newsitem.title: UK: Investors rush to buy Ford Motor Credit jumbo bond.
newsitem.headline: Investors rush to buy Ford Motor Credit jumbo bond.

text.p: Ford Motor Credit Corp's jumbo $1.25 billion global bond, launched on Thursday and priced on Friday, was hailed as a success as investors rushed to buy the high-yielding paper, bankers said.
"It's an extremely successful transaction, with very broad allocation around the world," an official at joint lead manager Goldman Sachs said.
"The deal was increased to $1.25 billion from $1.0 billion following strong demand. It was also priced at the tight end of the 38-39 basis point range," he said.
The A1/A+ rated Ford bond was priced to yield 38 b.p. over U.S. Treasury notes. By 1630 GMT it had tightened by 1/2 a basis point, dealers said.
Salomon Brothers was the other joint lead manager.
The Goldman Sachs official said over half their bonds had been sold outside of the U.S., with a particularly strong bid from Asia.
The Ford name, together with strong appetite for bonds that offered some yield in an environment where spreads continue falling, had driven strong demand for the deal.
"The success is partly a function of Ford's history and partly a function of the current situation where there is strong demand for higher-yielding paper," the Goldman official said.
"Ford has built up a very strong reputation in the market for the success of these transaction. Their global bonds have a good track record," he said.
Ford Motor Credit Corp last tapped the global dollar sector in September 1996, when it launched a $1.0 billion five-year global bond at a 48 b.p. spread to U.S. Treasury notes.

Last May it issued a $750 million five-year Euro-Asian bond, which has listings in Europe and Asia to appeal to investors in both regions. It first global was launched in 1995, also a $1.0 billion five-year issue, at 53 b.p. over Treasuries.
